_comment: Declarative GitHub repo-config baseline. Consumed by github-standard.py — see that file's header and docs/github-standard.md for the full rationale. Every override below carries a comment naming why; don't 'fix' a pinned exception back to the default without reading the linked doc first.
_profiles_comment: A profile describes the shape of a branch's review posture — not the repo's settings (those stay a repo-level settings_overrides, since GitHub settings aren't branch-scoped even when the policy driving them is). A repo/branch resolves to a profile explicitly ('profile': '<name>') or defaults to 'baseline'. Profile fields layer on top of defaults.ruleset the same way repo/branch overrides do: rule_overrides deep-merge into the matching default rule, extra_rules append, bypass_actors replace wholesale if set.

hobby._comment: Scratch/personal repos pushed to directly. No ruleset at all — just the settings+security baseline.

baseline._comment: The canonical shape: squash-only, 0 required approvals, required signatures, zero bypass. Used as-is by most repos; also the implicit default for any branch that doesn't name a profile.

oss._comment: Published, publicly-contributable projects (CODEOWNERS committed) — needs real review of external contributions, which baseline's 0-approval posture doesn't provide. bypass_actors lets the owner still merge their own PRs past a review requirement aimed at everyone else — look up the numeric RepositoryRole id for "admin"/"maintain" via GET /repos/{o}/{r}/rulesets/rule-suites or the ruleset UI.

flagship._comment: Multi-stage release branches on a repo with a real deploy pipeline (e.g. integration-branch -> main). A release promotion is a merge commit, never squash, because squash breaks ancestry between two long-lived branches: the merge-base never advances, so every later release PR shows a phantom diff of already-deployed code. Apply only to the release/main branch of a two-stage flow, not the integration branch feeding it — that one stays 'baseline' (squash).
